records.claim: \IEEEPARstart{I}{oT} topic namespaces expand with new devices, measurements and tenants. Monitoring clients may require future public topics while remaining excluded from private descendants. MQTT delivery combines subscription authorization, filter matching and receive authorization. P-Verifier analyzes the resulting effective cloud-IoT communication, including receive permissions~\cite{pverifier}. Exact-topic Denies can miss forbidden descendants; finite whitelists can block legitimate new branches (Figure~\ref{fig:problem_overview}). Both requirements therefore concern topic languages, not just currently enumerated topics.

Repair must distinguish a corrected policy from one that merely passes its listed examples. Unlike policy generation from natural-language requirements~\cite{sok_nl}, the task here takes explicit communication obligations as input. It poses two coupled challenges: preserving required communication while excluding forbidden languages, and ensuring that the resulting edit combination can be deployed. Deny-all and retaining every Allow fail opposite obligations. Moreover, language-equivalent rules can occupy different deployment keys; replacing one without its conflict context may discard an otherwise deployable repair.

Blockchain supports trustworthy digital-twin exchange~\cite{li_dt_survey}, ABE authorization~\cite{dt_abe} and information-centric services~\cite{icn_survey}. SPR-IoT repairs the static scope supplied to these mechanisms.

Let $\T$ contain nonempty printable-ASCII topics, at most 65,535 bytes, excluding literal \texttt{+}/\texttt{\#}. Each character occupies one byte. Empty levels and leading/trailing/repeated separators are supported. In $\Lang(f)\subseteq\T$, \texttt{+} matches one level, final \texttt{\#} all remaining levels; root wildcards exclude \texttt{\$}-prefixed topics. ASCII restricts the implementation, not MQTT~\cite{mqtt311}.

The offline AWS adapter treats resource \texttt{*}/\texttt{?} as string wildcards, unlike MQTT \texttt{+}/\texttt{\#}; \texttt{topicfilter}/\texttt{topic} authorize different events~\cite{aws_policy}. Its condition-free finite subset uses explicit-deny precedence. Variables, complex conditions, AWS-to-Mosquitto translation and full multi-policy composition~\cite{aws_engine} are unsupported.

Rule conversion can introduce explicit Denies~\cite{deny_conversion}; our edit grammar instead fixes the admissible changes and their deployment context. Original slots permit keep/delete and receive-Allow narrowing. Seeds use declared requests/requirements and fixed single-level/subtree generalizations, with symbolic containment checks. Additional slots permit forbidden-pattern receive denies above existing priorities. Identities, roles, defaults and original priorities are fixed.

Q requires equal event/effect/priority, receive languages (or decisions on $F$) and full unpruned conflict footprints, with nonincreasing additive cost~\cite{moito}. Absence merges only with itself; language/signature equality alone is insufficient.

The fixed P-Verifier source~\cite{pverifier_code} yields 541 unique whole documents from 834 JSON files and, separately, 547 unique Statement wrappers from 969 occurrences. Keys sort; arrays retain order. CloudFix has 276 unique/282 valid documents, 22 IoT-related. Researcher-supplemented B requirements give eleven overgrants (six P-Verifier policies, one template), five safe/two mixed-undergrant diagnoses.
